summary: A 19-foot brick tower on Hyannis Harbor, lit in 1849 as the back light of a range, dark since 1929 and privately owned.

structures.note: USLHS year 1849; LighthouseFriends gives an 1850 approval (see resolved_conflicts)

access.note: Privately owned and closed; USLHS lists it as not open to the public. Rowlett notes views from the street and from nearby Keyes Beach.

events.note: Daniel Snow Hallett privately established a light before the federal station; USLHS roster begins with Daniel S. Hallett in 1847
Congress appropriated $2,000 for a small harbor light on 14 August 1848
USLHS: year established 1849; original optic an oil lamp with reflector
James Bears appointed keeper 12 February 1849 at $350 a year
Fifth-order Fresnel lens replaced a system of five lamps in fourteen-inch reflectors (LighthouseFriends)
New cast-iron lantern placed atop the brick tower (LighthouseFriends)
Characteristic changed from fixed white to fixed red; Deyo (1890) describes a fixed red light
Front range beacon erected on the Old Colony Railroad wharf to range with the rear light; Rowlett dates the range from 1885
Range beacon, not the rear tower, almost entirely rebuilt after storms (LighthouseFriends)
Summer kitchen and fuel-house added to the dwelling
Iron deck and wooden parapet replaced the wooden deck and brick parapet
Decommissioned when the main wharf moved to Lewis Bay; USLHS and Rowlett give 1929
Lantern room removed from the inactive tower
New, not quite traditional, lantern room placed atop the tower (LighthouseFriends dates it 1986)
Red bands added when the tower was repainted

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends dates the change from fixed white to fixed red to 1878; Deyo's 1890 history describes a fixed red light, so the characteristic recorded here is fixed red after 1878. The 1848 appropriation, as LighthouseFriends reports it, mentions a fixed white light with a red sector; this is not reconciled with the later description.
The USLHS record gives the keeper's quarters year as 1849. LighthouseFriends says $800 was approved for a keeper's house on 28 September 1850. Not reconciled; the story gives both.
LighthouseFriends dates a new, not quite traditional lantern room to 1986. Rowlett says the lantern removed in 1929 was replaced by an octagonal sunroom (1989). Not reconciled; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Keeper years are the USLHS roster's own; LighthouseFriends agrees with every year it gives. Wikipedia (not cited) gives different dates and spellings (Daniel Snow Hallett 1849-1851, James Bearse 1851-1853, Franklin Baker 1861-1869, John Lothrop 1869-1878); left out, the roster kept. Tower height: Deyo's 1890 history gives 21 ft (tower); USLHS and Rowlett give 19 ft (base to lantern centre); both are quoted in the story and unresolved. Lantern date: LighthouseFriends says 1986; Wikipedia (not cited) says 1987. The 1848 appropriation and Pleasonton's words are second-hand through LighthouseFriends; the Congressional and Light-House Board records of 1848-1867 are not in the local corpus, and the corpus Light-House Board reports start in 1891 and mention Hyannis only in buoy, light-vessel and tender lines. The Deyo 'Hyannis Beacon light' is probably the 1885 wharf beacon; Deyo does not say so (stated as our inference in the story). Chronicling America searches for the station, the keepers and the range light (Massachusetts papers, 1840-1930) found nothing usable. The Hyannis Patriot article of 3 March 1927 that LighthouseFriends cites was not accessible. The USCG Historian's page (archived copies) returned 403 and was not used. The keepers' names and years were not matched against any table by column position. The 1881 instructions are OCR-garbled mid-sentence; the evidence quotes are split at an ellipsis, each part verified by hand. Owners of the private keeper's house are deliberately not named. Daniel Bunker Hallet, the child who helped with the lamp, is in the story only, not in the roster. No new photos were found. Added to the story text this round: the keeper's quarters year (USLHS 1849 against LighthouseFriends' September 1850 approval) and the lantern (LighthouseFriends' 1986 lantern room against Rowlett's 1989 octagonal sunroom); both are stated as unresolved. The 1881 General Instructions rule 4 was checked on the page image (archive.org/details/1881USLH, scan p.3, printed p.5): visit at least twice between 8 p.m. and sunrise, and constant attention on stormy nights, with no assistant.
